requirements.text: In height, the rear position lamp shall be not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
requirements.why: This mounting height limit applies to the mandatory rear position lamps.
requirements.test_case: Measure the height of the apparent surface above ground on the unladen vehicle and verify it is within 350–1,500 mm (or ≤ 2,100 mm where justified).

requirements.text: In length, the rear position lamp shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: This longitudinal position requirement applies to the rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle to confirm the lamps are located at the rear.

requirements.text: The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall cover a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
requirements.why: This sets the horizontal geometric visibility of the installed rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility of the apparent surface over 45° inwards and 80° outwards (20° inwards below the H plane if mounted below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall cover a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.why: This sets the vertical geometric visibility of the installed rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility over ±15° vertically (5° downward if mounted below 750 mm).

requirements.text: For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1 and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the horizontal angle of geometric visibility shall be 45° outwards to 45° inwards; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
requirements.why: This alternative horizontal visibility applies to M1 vehicles fitted with a rear side-marker lamp.
requirements.test_case: Where a rear side-marker lamp is fitted and this alternative is chosen, verify visibility from 45° outwards to 45° inwards.

requirements.text: For M1 category vehicles using the alternative visibility of paragraph 6.10.5.2, the vertical angle shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.why: This alternative vertical visibility applies to M1 vehicles using the 6.10.5.2 option.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility over ±15° vertically (5° downward if mounted below 750 mm) under the alternative option.

requirements.text: To be considered visible, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
requirements.why: This visibility criterion applies to the rear position lamp, which is grouped with a retro-reflector in this product.
requirements.test_case: Measure the unobstructed projected apparent surface at the visibility angles, excluding non-transmitting retro-reflector area, and verify it is ≥ 12.5 cm².

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
requirements.why: This orientation requirement applies to the installed rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installation to confirm the lamp reference axis points rearwards.

requirements.text: The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11, such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps and side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
requirements.why: This electrical connection rule applies to the rear position lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lighting switch and verify the rear position lamps switch ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position and registration plate lamps.

requirements.text: A closed-circuit tell-tale shall be mandatory for the rear position lamp, except when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
requirements.why: A tell-tale is required for the rear position lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Switch on the position lamps and verify the closed-circuit tell-tale illuminates.

requirements.text: The tell-tale of the rear position lamp shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
requirements.why: This tell-tale combination requirement applies to the rear position lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Verify the same tell-tale indicates operation of both the front and rear position lamps.

requirements.text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
requirements.why: The LED rear position lamp may require failure indication under the component Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Check whether R7/R148 requires a failure indication for this LED lamp and, if so, simulate failure and verify the tell-tale activates.

requirements.text: The rear non-triangular retro-reflector shall be present on motor vehicles (mandatory on M1).
requirements.why: M1 is a motor vehicle and the lamp provides the rear retro-reflector function.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle rear for presence of the rear retro-reflectors.

requirements.text: The number of rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be two.
requirements.why: Fixes the quantity of the retro-reflector function installed via this lamp pair.
requirements.test_case: Count the rear retro-reflectors fitted on the vehicle (one per side lamp).

requirements.text: The rear retro-reflectors shall be type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.
requirements.why: P-05 is a Class IA retro-reflector and must carry the referenced approval.
requirements.test_case: Verify the R3/R150 Class IA approval marking on the retro-reflector.

requirements.text: Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
requirements.why: Conditions any additional retro-reflecting parts integrated in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect any additional retro-reflecting elements and check that mandatory lamps remain unobstructed and photometrically compliant.

requirements.text: In width, the point on the illuminating surface of the retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Position constraint on the retro-reflector placed within the rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lateral distance from the outermost illuminating-surface point to the vehicle's extreme outer edge.

requirements.text: In height, the retro-reflector shall be not less than 250 mm above the ground.
requirements.why: Mounting height constraint for the retro-reflector in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lowest point of the illuminating surface height above ground in unladen condition.

requirements.text: In height, the retro-reflector shall be not more than 900 mm above the ground, or not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), or 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector is grouped with rear lamps in this combination lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure the highest point of the illuminating surface above ground and compare with the applicable limit (grouped: 1,200 mm).

requirements.text: In length, the retro-reflector shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Longitudinal position requirement for the rear retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Inspect installation position on the vehicle rear.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall have geometric visibility over a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards.
requirements.why: Visibility requirement for the installed retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Check unobstructed visibility of the illuminating surface over ±30° horizontally on the installed lamp.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall have geometric visibility over a vertical angle of 10° above and below horizontal, except that where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane) the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.why: Vertical visibility requirement for the installed retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Check unobstructed visibility over 10° up and 10° down (5° down if mounted below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.
requirements.why: Orientation requirement for the rear retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that the reference axis of the retro-reflector points rearwards when installed.

requirements.text: Any vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6. (including the installation requirements for the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors).
requirements.why: The rear lamp installed on an M1 vehicle must remain conforming to the approved installation type in series production.
requirements.test_case: Conformity of production audit: check series-production vehicles with the fitted rear lamp against the installation requirements of paragraphs 5 and 6 and the approved type.

requirements.text: The position of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors in width, height and length shall be such that the measured distances fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
requirements.why: The CoP check of the lamp's mounting position applies to each rear lamp function fitted on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the mounting width, height and length positions of each function on production vehicles and compare them with the paragraph 6 limits.

requirements.text: The measured angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, with an allowance on the angle limits corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3.
requirements.why: The CoP visibility check applies to each rear signalling function of the product.
requirements.test_case: Measure the geometric visibility angles of each lamp function on production vehicles.

requirements.text: The visibility of white light towards the rear (other than from the reversing lamp) and of red light towards the front shall comply with paragraph 5.10.
requirements.why: The red rear lamp and the white reversing lamp section are subject to the paragraph 5.10 visibility checks.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the vehicle to confirm no red light from the rear lamp is visible to the front and no white light other than the reversing lamp's is visible to the rear.

requirements.text: When every lamp supplied by the vehicle electrical system is switched on, the rear position lamps, stop lamps and reversing lamps and their tell-tales shall function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
requirements.why: The electrical connections of the lamp's functions are checked at CoP.
requirements.test_case: Switch on each function on a production vehicle and verify correct operation and electrical connection, including tell-tales.

requirements.text: The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, category of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors, as checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall fulfil paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
requirements.why: The colour, number and markings of the lamp functions are verified at CoP.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the lamp colours (red/white), the number of lamps, the arrangement and the approval markings on production vehicles.

requirements.text: Where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and the apparent surface "7b" is based on the light-emitting surface according to paragraph 2.10.2. (b), function F1 (e.g. rear position lamp) shall not be transparent to function F2 (e.g. stop lamp or reversing lamp) in the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated rear lamp.
requirements.why: The rear lamp groups several functions behind one outer lens, so this Part 7 configuration constraint applies when the light-emitting surface is declared under 2.10.2. (b).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and the sample with each function lit separately to confirm that light from F2 does not pass through the optical part of F1.

requirements.text: For each single-function lamp with a reflector optic, inner lens or light guide behind an outer lens, the illuminating surface and the light-emitting surface shall be determined consistent with the examples of Annex 3 Part 5 (Examples 1 to 9).
requirements.why: These figures set how the surfaces of the rear position, stop and reversing lamps are taken for installation and visibility checks.
requirements.test_case: Compare the illuminating and light-emitting surfaces on the approval drawing with Annex 3 Part 5, Examples 1 to 9.

requirements.text: Where the outer lens is textured, the light-emitting surface shall include the outer lens (Examples 1, 3 and 5). Where the outer lens is non-textured, it may be excluded and the light-emitting surface declared on the drawing (Examples 2, 4 and 6).
requirements.why: The product has a full-cover PMMA outer lens over reflector optics, so the outer-lens treatment determines the declared surfaces.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer lens for texture in each function zone and check that the declared light-emitting surface matches the applicable example.

requirements.text: Where a lamp's reflector optic is combined, behind the outer lens, with an area that is not part of that function, that area shall be excluded from that function's illuminating and light-emitting surface (Example 9).
requirements.why: The combination lamp shares one outer lens across several functions and compartments.
requirements.test_case: Check on the drawing that the retro-reflector, reversing and other-function zones are excluded from each function's declared surfaces.

requirements.text: When determining the illuminating surface of the rear lamp functions (rear position, stop, reversing lamp), any area of the lens/housing which is not part of the function concerned shall be excluded, the edges of the illuminating surface being defined as shown in Example C.
requirements.why: The installed lamp's illuminating surface feeds R48 position and geometric-visibility checks, so it must be determined as illustrated.
requirements.test_case: Review the declared illuminating-surface drawing for each function and confirm that adjacent non-functional areas are excluded as per Example C.

requirements.text: Where the light-emitting surface is declared according to paragraph 2.10.2. (a), it shall be delimited by the declared edges (c-d and e-f) and shall exclude any area which is not part of the function, as shown in Example D.
requirements.why: The declared light-emitting surface of the rear lamp functions is used for installation and visibility assessment.
requirements.test_case: Compare the manufacturer's declared light-emitting surface drawing with the lamp and verify that non-functional areas are excluded as per Example D.

requirements.text: Where the outer lens is non-textured and the light-emitting surface is declared according to paragraph 2.10.2. (b), the light-emitting surface shall be determined from the apparent surface, delimited by the declared edges (c'-d' and e'-f') and excluding any area which is not part of the function, as shown in Example E.
requirements.why: Applies to the rear lamp's outer lens zones when they are non-textured and the surface is declared under 2.10.2. (b).
requirements.test_case: For non-textured lens zones, verify that the declared light-emitting surface is derived from the apparent surface and excludes non-functional areas as per Example E.

requirements.text: In the case where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and "7b" is taken as the apparent surface according to paragraph 2.10.2., the lamp function F1 shall not be transparent to the lamp function F2.
requirements.why: The rear lamp groups several functions (position, stop, reversing) behind one outer lens, so the apparent-surface layout rule applies to its compartments.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and the sample to confirm that, where the apparent surface of one function (e.g. stop lamp) lies behind another (e.g. rear position lamp), the light of F2 is not transmitted through F1.

requirements.text: In the case of a textured outer lens, the light emitting surface and apparent surface of each lamp function shall be determined with the outer lens included. This also applies where a wall separates the functions.
requirements.why: The product's red PMMA outer lens has a ribbed (textured) zone, and the housing has partition walls between the functions.
requirements.test_case: Check that the declared light emitting surfaces on the approval drawing are on the exterior of the textured outer lens and are bounded by the internal partition walls.

requirements.text: For verifying that red light is not visible from the front and white light (other than from the reversing lamp) is not visible from the rear (paragraph 5.10.4.), the observation zones 1 and 2 shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.
requirements.why: The rear lamp emits red light and white reversing light, so its installation must satisfy the visibility checks performed within these zones.
requirements.test_case: With the lamp installed on the vehicle, check from observer positions between 1 m and 2.2 m height that no red light is visible from the front zone and no non-permitted white light from the rear zone.

requirements.text: The observation zones 1 and 2 shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width.
requirements.why: These zone limits determine where the lamp's red light must not be visible from the front.
requirements.test_case: Lay out the 15° outward boundary planes from the vehicle width contact points and verify that no red light from the rear lamp is visible within the front zone 1.

requirements.text: If there are several points of contact delimiting the vehicle's overall width, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.
requirements.why: Defines the zone geometry against which the wraparound rear lamp's light visibility is verified.
requirements.test_case: Identify the foremost and rearmost width contact points on the vehicle and use them to construct the front and rear zone boundaries for the visibility check.

requirements.text: For the tests verifying the position and orientation of the lamps on the M1 vehicle, the mass of the passengers shall be calculated on the basis of 75 kg per person.
requirements.why: This is a general loading rule in Annex 5 that applies to any lamp position or orientation check on the M1 vehicle carrying the rear lamp; the remaining Annex 5 paragraphs apply only to dipped-beam headlamps, which this product does not have.
requirements.test_case: Check the test report to confirm that each occupant in the loading conditions was simulated with 75 kg when lamp position and orientation were verified.

requirements.text: For conformity of production, the position of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors in width, in height and in length shall be checked in accordance with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of this Regulation.
requirements.why: The rear lamp functions installed on the M1 vehicle are subject to position checks in CoP.
requirements.test_case: Measure lamp positions on a production M1 vehicle, unladen on a flat horizontal surface, relative to the declared surfaces and extreme outer edge.

requirements.text: The values measured for the distances (width, height, length) of each lamp shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, rear retro-reflector) are fulfilled.
requirements.why: The installed rear lamp's position must meet the individual specifications for its functions.
requirements.test_case: Compare the measured mounting distances against the limits of the individual lamp specifications in paragraph 6.

requirements.text: The angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7. of this Regulation.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility of the installed rear lamp functions is verified in CoP.
requirements.test_case: Determine the horizontal and vertical visibility angles of the apparent surface of each function on the vehicle.

requirements.text: The values measured for the angles of geometric visibility shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
requirements.why: The visibility angles of the rear lamp's signalling functions must meet the lamp-specific values.
requirements.test_case: Verify the measured visibility angles meet the lamp-specific angles within a ±3° allowance.

requirements.text: The visibility of red light towards the front from the rear position lamp, stop lamp and red retro-reflector shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation, and the red light shall not be visible towards the front beyond what is permitted there.
requirements.why: The rear lamp emits/reflects red light that must not be visible to the front.
requirements.test_case: Inspect from the front zone defined in paragraph 5.10 that no direct red light from the rear lamp is visible.

requirements.text: The visibility of white light towards the rear from the reversing lamp shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.
requirements.why: The rear lamp contains a white reversing lamp emitting to the rear.
requirements.test_case: Verify the white light to the rear comes only from the reversing lamp, as permitted by paragraph 5.10.

requirements.text: The electrical connections shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle, including the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp.
requirements.why: The rear lamp functions are supplied by the vehicle electrical system.
requirements.test_case: Switch on each function on the vehicle and confirm that it lights.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
requirements.why: The switching behaviour of the rear lamp functions is verified in CoP.
requirements.test_case: Verify the switching logic of each lamp, e.g. rear position lamps switch ON/OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps and registration plate lamp, the stop lamp lights on service-brake application, and the reversing lamp lights only with reverse gear engaged.

requirements.text: The tell-tales associated with the rear lamp functions, where required, shall function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
requirements.why: Tell-tale operation linked to the installed rear lamp functions is checked in CoP.
requirements.test_case: Operate the functions and check the tell-tale behaviour, where a tell-tale is required.

requirements.text: The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings.
requirements.why: The rear lamp's functions and markings are visually verified in CoP.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the vehicle lamps and their approval markings.

requirements.text: The presence, number, colour, arrangement and category of lamps shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraph 5.15. (colours) are fulfilled: rear position lamp red, stop lamp red, reversing lamp white, rear non-triangular retro-reflector red.
requirements.why: The colours of the rear lamp's functions must conform to paragraph 5.15.
requirements.test_case: Verify the colour of each function visually and by marking (red for position, stop and retro-reflector; white for reversing).

requirements.text: The presence, number and arrangement of the lamps shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraph 5.16. (number of lamps) as well as the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
requirements.why: The number and arrangement of the installed rear lamp functions are checked against the Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Count the installed rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors and compare them with the required numbers.

requirements.text: The markings of the lamps (approval markings, including category where applicable) shall be present and consistent with the lamps installed, such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
requirements.why: Lamp markings are the basis of the CoP visual inspection of the rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the approval markings on the rear lamp lens/housing for each function and the retro-reflector class (IA).

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the LED light source shall bear on the cap the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.why: Applies to any replaceable LED light source fitted in the rear lamp, which must be approved under R128.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the LED light source cap for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the LED light source shall bear on the cap the rated voltage.
requirements.why: Marking obligation on a replaceable LED light source used in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the cap for the rated voltage marking.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the LED light source shall bear on the cap the designation of the relevant category.
requirements.why: Marking obligation on a replaceable LED light source used in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the cap for the R128 category designation.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the LED light source shall bear on the cap a space of sufficient size to accommodate the approval mark.
requirements.why: Design obligation on the cap of a replaceable LED light source used in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the cap and drawings to confirm a space large enough for the approval mark.

requirements.text: In the case of LED substitute light sources, the LED light source shall bear on the cap the symbol ISO 7000, symbol 1641.
requirements.why: Applies if an LED substitute light source is used as a replaceable source in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the cap of an LED substitute light source for ISO 7000 symbol 1641.

requirements.text: Inscriptions on the LED light source other than those covered by paragraphs 2.3.1. and 2.4.4. shall not adversely affect the luminous characteristics.
requirements.why: Constrains any additional markings on a replaceable LED light source used in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Compare photometric measurements of the light source with and without additional inscriptions, or inspect inscription location relative to the light-emitting area.

requirements.text: Each LED light source sample shall conform to the relevant specifications of this Regulation (applicable only if replaceable LED light sources are used).
requirements.why: Applies to any replaceable LED light source (e.g. LR/LW categories) used in the rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Check every sample against all applicable R128 provisions and the relevant Annex 1 data sheet.

requirements.text: LED light sources shall be so designed as to be and to remain in good working order when in normal use.
requirements.why: Design durability obligation on any approved LED light source fitted in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect samples and check function after the ageing and test sequence.

requirements.text: LED light sources shall exhibit no fault in design or manufacture.
requirements.why: Construction quality obligation on the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Visually and functionally inspect samples for design or manufacturing defects.

requirements.text: LED light sources shall exhibit no scores or spots on their optical surfaces which might impair their efficiency and their optical performance; this shall be verified when commencing approval testing and when required in the respective paragraphs.
requirements.why: Optical surface quality requirement for the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect optical surfaces before testing and after the maximum-temperature test sequence.

requirements.text: LED light sources shall be equipped with standard caps complying with the cap data sheets of IEC Publication 60061 as specified on the individual data sheets of Annex 1.
requirements.why: Cap interface requirement for a replaceable LED light source in the lamp holder.
requirements.test_case: Perform a dimension check and trial fitting into the IEC 60061 holder.

requirements.text: The cap shall be strong and firmly secured to the rest of the LED light source.
requirements.why: Mechanical construction rule for the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect and manually check the cap-to-body attachment.

requirements.text: Conformity with paragraphs 3.2.3 to 3.2.5 shall be verified by a visual inspection, a dimension check and, where necessary, a trial fitting into the holder as specified in IEC Publication 60061.
requirements.why: Defines the verification method for the cap and surface requirements.
requirements.test_case: Perform the visual inspection, dimension check and holder trial fitting.

requirements.text: The solid state junction(s) and possibly one or more elements for fluorescence-based conversion shall be the only element(s) of the LED light source that generate(s) and emit(s) light when energized.
requirements.why: Design rule on the light-generating elements of the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the construction and energize the source to confirm no other light-emitting elements.

requirements.text: LED light sources shall first be aged at their test voltage for at least forty-eight hours before testing.
requirements.why: Test pre-conditioning that constrains the product's verification.
requirements.test_case: Age the samples for 48 h or more at test voltage before measurements.

requirements.text: For multi-function LED light sources, each function shall be aged separately.
requirements.why: Applies to dual-function sources such as stop/position LED sources.
requirements.test_case: Age each function (e.g. major/minor) separately for 48 h or more.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, electrical and photometric measurements shall be carried out at the relevant test voltage(s).
requirements.why: Test condition for the product's electrical and photometric verification.
requirements.test_case: Set the supply to the test voltage (e.g. 13.5 V DC) for measurements.

requirements.text: Electrical measurements as specified in Annex 4 shall be carried out with instruments of at least class 0.2 (0.2 per cent full scale accuracy).
requirements.why: Measurement accuracy condition for verifying the source's electrical values.
requirements.test_case: Check calibration certificates of the measuring instruments.

requirements.text: The position and dimensions of the light emitting area shall conform to the requirements as given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
requirements.why: Geometric optical requirement for the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Perform the screen projection box-system test per the category sheet.

requirements.text: The light emitting area position and dimension measurement shall be made after ageing the LED light source according to 3.3.1.
requirements.why: Test condition for the light emitting area verification.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the 48 h ageing was completed before the box measurement.

requirements.text: When measured according to the conditions specified in Annex 4, the luminous flux shall be within the limits given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
requirements.why: Photometric flux limit for the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous flux with an integrating sphere at test voltage after 1 min and 30 min.

requirements.text: The luminous flux measurement shall be made after ageing the LED light source according to 3.3.1.
requirements.why: Test condition for the luminous flux verification.
requirements.test_case: Confirm ageing was completed before the flux measurement.

requirements.text: When measured according to the test conditions specified in Annex 4, the normalized luminous intensity distribution and/or cumulative luminous flux distribution shall be within the limits given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
requirements.why: Angular radiation pattern requirement for the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Perform goniophotometer measurement in the specified C-planes and normalise to 1000 lm.

requirements.text: The intensity distribution measurement shall be made after ageing the LED light source according to 3.3.1.
requirements.why: Test condition for the intensity distribution verification.
requirements.test_case: Confirm ageing was completed before the goniometric measurement.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the LED light sources shall be as specified on the relevant data sheet (red for rear position/stop, white for reversing), with colour definitions per Regulation No. 48.
requirements.why: Colour requirement for the red and white LED sources in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Compare the measured chromaticity with the data-sheet colour.

requirements.text: When measured by the method specified in Annex 4, the measured integral value of the chromaticity coordinates shall lie within the required chromaticity area.
requirements.why: Colorimetric limit for the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Measure integral chromaticity x,y with a spectroradiometer and check against the R48 colour boundaries.

requirements.text: In the case of LED light sources emitting white light, the minimum red content of the light shall meet the specified formula, calculated using intervals of one nanometer.
requirements.why: Applies to the white reversing-lamp LED source.
requirements.test_case: Compute the red content from the measured spectral irradiance at 1 nm steps.

requirements.text: The UV-radiation of the LED light source shall be such that the LED light source is of the low UV type complying with the specified formula, weighted by S(λ) per the table, with km = 683 lm/W and calculated using intervals of one nanometer.
requirements.why: UV emission limit applies to every LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Measure the spectral distribution 250-400 nm, apply the S(λ) weighting and compute against the low-UV limit.

requirements.text: Where a maximum test temperature is specified on the data sheet, when measured according to Annex 4 paragraph 5, the luminous flux values at elevated temperatures shall be within the limits given in the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
requirements.why: Thermal photometric requirement when the category specifies a maximum test temperature.
requirements.test_case: Measure flux in steps of 25 °C or less up to the maximum test temperature.

requirements.text: Where a maximum test temperature is specified on the data sheet, when measured according to Annex 4 paragraph 5, the colour variation shall not exceed 0.010.
requirements.why: Thermal colour stability requirement.
requirements.test_case: Compute the maximum chromaticity deviation from the 23 °C/Tb reference point.

requirements.text: After the measurement of 3.10.1, the LED light source shall be continuously operated during 1000 h at the relevant test voltage(s), at an ambient temperature equal to the maximum test temperature (integrated heatsink) or at a Tb-value equal to the maximum test temperature (specified Tb-point).
requirements.why: Endurance condition the source must withstand when a maximum test temperature is specified.
requirements.test_case: Run the 1000 h endurance at maximum test temperature.

requirements.text: After the 1000 h operation, the luminous flux values at elevated temperatures shall not deviate by more than ± 10 per cent from the corresponding values of the individual sample measured according to paragraph 3.10.1.
requirements.why: Flux maintenance requirement after thermal endurance.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the elevated-temperature flux measurement and compare with the initial values.

requirements.text: After the 1000 h operation, the colour variation shall not deviate from the corresponding values of the individual sample measured according to paragraph 3.10.1 by more than ± 0.010.
requirements.why: Colour stability requirement after thermal endurance.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the colour variation measurement and compare with the initial values.

requirements.text: After completion of the measurement procedure of paragraph 3.10.3, the LED light source shall again exhibit no scores or spots on its optical surfaces which might impair its efficiency and optical performance (3.2.3).
requirements.why: Post-endurance surface integrity check on the LED light source.
requirements.test_case: Visually re-inspect optical surfaces after the endurance sequence.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources approved to UN R128 are used in the lamp, the LED light sources shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the inscriptions and technical requirements set forth in paragraph 3. and Annexes 1, 4 and 5 to this Regulation.
requirements.why: This applies only if the lamp uses replaceable R128 LED light sources (to be confirmed); it then binds their series production.
requirements.test_case: Take random production LED light sources and check markings, dimensions, electrical and photometric values against the Annex 1 data sheet tolerances for production light sources and the Annex 5 and Annex 6 acceptance criteria.

requirements.text: Where LED substitute light sources are concerned, the information on the packages and the instructions contained by the packages shall conform to the requirements as set forth in paragraph 4.
requirements.why: This is a borderline item: it applies only if replaceable LED substitute light sources are supplied with or for the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the packaging and enclosed instructions of production LED substitute light sources for the information required by paragraph 4.

requirements.text: Where a replaceable LED light source is used in the lamp, the sheets of the relevant LED light source category and the group in which this category is listed with restrictions on its use shall apply as incorporated in Resolution R.E.5 or its subsequent revisions, applicable at the time of application for type approval of the LED light source.
requirements.why: Applies only if the profile's 'presumed non-replaceable' LED modules turn out to be replaceable LED light sources (confirm).
requirements.test_case: Check the LED light source category and its R.E.5 group restrictions against the rear position, stop and reversing functions.

requirements.text: For category LR1, dimension e shall be 24.0 mm with a tolerance of ±0.2 mm for LED light sources of normal production (±0.1 mm for standard LED light sources).
requirements.why: Red LR1 sources are a candidate for the rear position/stop functions.
requirements.test_case: Measure dimension e on production samples.

requirements.text: For category LR1, the cap shall be PGJ21t-1 in accordance with IEC Publication 60061 (sheet 7004-165-1).
requirements.why: Cap interchangeability of an LR1 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Gauge the cap against IEC 60061 sheet 7004-165-1.

requirements.text: For category LR1, at 13.5 V DC after 30 minutes continuous operation at 23 ± 2.5 °C, the wattage shall be 0.75 W max. for the minor function and 3.5 W max. / 1.4 W min. for the major function, at a rated voltage of 12 V.
requirements.why: Electrical limit of an LR1 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure power after 30 min of stabilisation at 13.5 V DC.

requirements.text: For category LR1 LED light sources of normal production, the luminous flux at 10-16 V DC shall be 3.5 lm ± 20 % for the minor function and 47 lm ± 20 % for the major function (standard light sources: 3.5 lm ± 10 % and 47 lm ± 10 % at 13.5 V DC).
requirements.why: Photometric limit of an LR1 source used for position/stop.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous flux in an integrating sphere over 10-16 V DC.

requirements.text: For category LR1, in case of LED light source failure (no light emitted), the maximum current draw when operated within the input voltage range in major function mode shall be less than 20 mA (open circuit condition).
requirements.why: Failure behaviour of an LR1 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Simulate an LED failure and measure the current draw across the voltage range.

requirements.text: For category LR1, at least 95 per cent of the luminous flux emitted into the viewing direction shall come from the trapezoidal area defined by d1, d2 and c of the box system (Figure 3, Table 2).
requirements.why: Light emitting area position of an LR1 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a screen projection with the box system and evaluate the flux fractions.

requirements.text: For category LR1, less than 70 per cent of the luminous flux shall be emitted from the rectangular area defined by d3 and c (normal production: f = e+0.2, c = 3.6, d1 = 21.0, d2 = 15.0, d3 = 7.0 mm).
requirements.why: Light emitting area constraint of an LR1 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a screen projection and measure the flux from the d3×c rectangle.

requirements.text: For category LR1, the emitted light shall be red.
requirements.why: Colour of an LR1 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates.

requirements.text: For category LR1, the normalized luminous intensity of the major function, measured in 3 C-planes within C30 and C330 at least 30° apart and normalized to 1000 lm, shall comply with the Table 3 tolerance band for normal production (e.g. γ=0°: 0-30; 45°: 20-100; 90°: 70-160; 120°/135°: 110-200; 150°: 90-180 cd/1000 lm).
requirements.why: Intensity distribution of an LR1 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a goniophotometer measurement and compare against Table 3.

requirements.text: For category LR1, the luminous intensity distribution shall be substantially uniform, i.e. between two adjacent grid points the requirement is calculated by linear interpolation.
requirements.why: Uniformity of an LR1 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Check interpolated values between the grid points.

requirements.text: For category LW2, dimension e shall be 26.4 mm with a tolerance of ±0.2 mm for normal production (±0.1 mm for standard LED light sources), and the cap shall be PGJY50 in accordance with IEC Publication 60061 (sheet 7004-182-1).
requirements.why: White LW2 source is a candidate for the reversing lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure dimension e and gauge the cap.

requirements.text: For category LW2, at 13.5 V DC the wattage shall be 1 W max. for the minor function and 12 W max. / 4 W min. for the major function, at a rated voltage of 12 V.
requirements.why: Electrical limit of an LW2 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure power after 30 min with base temperature stabilised.

requirements.text: For category LW2 LED light sources of normal production, the luminous flux at 10-16 V DC shall be 50 lm ± 15 % (minor) and 725 lm ± 15 % (major), at base temperature Tb of 30 ± 2 °C (minor) and 55 ± 2 °C (major), after 30 minutes of continuous operation.
requirements.why: Photometric limit of an LW2 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure flux within ±40° α/β with Tb stabilised.

requirements.text: For category LW2, the emitted light shall be white.
requirements.why: Colour for the reversing function.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates.

requirements.text: For category LW2 LED light sources of normal production, the light emitting area shall comply with the box dimensions of Table 2: e = 26.4 ± 0.2, a = 14.5 +0/-2.5, b = 10.1 +0/-1.5, c = Ø 50.00 +0.10/-0 mm.
requirements.why: Light emitting area of an LW2 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a screen projection along the reference axis with a ±40° aperture.

requirements.text: For category LW2, the normalized cumulative luminous flux shall comply with Table 3 (±5°: 8-14 %; ±10°: 31-37 %; ±15°: 54-59 %; ±20°: 75-81 %; ±25°: 91-95 %; ±30°: 97-100 %; ±35°: 98-100 %).
requirements.why: Flux distribution of an LW2 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Record goniophotometer data at ≤1° steps and compute the cumulative flux per CIE 84.

requirements.text: For category LW2, the luminous flux determined independently for all 4 quadrants within each solid angle of Table 3 shall not differ by more than 15 %.
requirements.why: Symmetry requirement of an LW2 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Compare the quadrant flux values.

requirements.text: For category LW2, the thermal interface shall be attached to an appropriate heat sink or thermal management system, and the luminous flux of Table 1 shall be achieved once the base temperature Tb is stabilised.
requirements.why: The lamp housing must provide the thermal management for an LW2 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the heat sink attachment and measure flux at stabilised Tb.

requirements.text: For categories LR3A, LR3B, LW3A and LW3B, a minimum free air space of 5 mm around the light source shall be respected for convection.
requirements.why: Installation constraint on the lamp housing for an L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the clearance around the light source in the lamp housing.

requirements.text: For categories LR3A/LR3B/LW3A/LW3B, the dimensions shall be: a 6.0 mm max.; b c + 10.0 mm min., 38.0 mm max.; c 18.5 ± 0.1 mm; d 28.0 mm max.; e 3.0 ± 0.30 mm (standard 3.0 ± 0.15 mm); h 5.5 +0.0/-0.1 mm.
requirements.why: Dimensions of an L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a dimensional inspection.

requirements.text: The cap shall be PGJ18.5d-1 for LR3A/LR3B and PGJ18.5d-24 for LW3A/LW3B, in accordance with IEC Publication 60061 (sheet 7004-185-1).
requirements.why: Cap of an L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Gauge the cap.

requirements.text: For LR3A/LR3B, the rated values shall be 12 V and 3 W, and the objective wattage at 13.5 V DC shall be 3.5 W max. after 30 minutes of continuous operation at 23 ± 2.5 °C.
requirements.why: Electrical limit of a red L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the power.

requirements.text: For LR3A/LR3B, the luminous flux shall be 80 lm ± 20 % at 13.5 V DC (production), with the measured value between 100 and 70 per cent of the value measured after 1 minute, and 19 lm min. at 9 V DC.
requirements.why: Photometric limit of a red L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the flux at 1 min and at 30 min, and at 9 V DC.

requirements.text: For LW3A/LW3B, the rated values shall be 12 V and 4 W, and the wattage at 13.5 V DC shall be 5 W max.
requirements.why: Electrical limit of a white L3 source (reversing) if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the power.

requirements.text: For LW3A/LW3B, the luminous flux shall be 250 lm ± 20 % at 13.5 V DC (production) and 50 lm min. at 9 V DC.
requirements.why: Photometric limit of a white L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the flux.

requirements.text: The emitted light shall be red for LR3A/LR3B and white for LW3A/LW3B.
requirements.why: Colour of an L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity.

requirements.text: For categories L3, in case of LED light source failure (no light emitted), the max. electrical current draw when operated between 12 V and 14 V shall be less than 20 mA (open circuit condition).
requirements.why: Failure behaviour of an L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a failure and measure the current at 12-14 V.

requirements.text: For LR3A/LR3B LED light sources of normal production (box f = 3.0 mm), the flux proportion shall be: area A ≤ 25 %; each B individually ≥ 15 %; A, all B and all C together ≥ 90 %.
requirements.why: Light emitting area of a red L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a screen projection with the box system along γ=0°.

requirements.text: For LW3A/LW3B LED light sources of normal production (box f = 4.5 mm), the flux proportion shall be: each A, B individually ≥ 6 % and < 40 %; all A, B together ≥ 55 %; each C individually < 15 %; all A, B and C together ≥ 90 %.
requirements.why: Light emitting area of a white L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a screen projection with the box system.

requirements.text: For LR3A/LR3B, the normalized luminous intensity in C-planes C0 and C90 shall comply with Table 4a for normal production (e.g. 0°: 200-401; ±45°: 142-305; ±60°: 98-246; ±75°: 0-160; ±90°: 0-38 cd/1000 lm).
requirements.why: Intensity distribution of a red L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a goniophotometer measurement normalised to 1000 lm.

requirements.text: For LW3A/LW3B, the normalized luminous intensity shall comply with Table 4b for normal production (e.g. 0°: 200-425; ±45°: 145-310; ±60°: 85-245; ±75°: 0-160; ±90°: 0-70 cd/1000 lm).
requirements.why: Intensity distribution of a white L3 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a goniophotometer measurement.

requirements.text: For categories L3, LR4 and L5, the light pattern shall be substantially uniform, with requirements between adjacent grid points calculated by linear interpolation.
requirements.why: Uniformity of these sources if used.
requirements.test_case: Check interpolation between the grid points.

requirements.text: For LR4A/LR4B, a minimum free air space of 5 mm around the light source shall be respected for convection, and the cap shall be PGJ18.5t-5 in accordance with IEC Publication 60061 (sheet 7004-185-1).
requirements.why: A dual-function red LR4 source suits a combined position/stop lamp, if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the clearance and gauge the cap.

requirements.text: For LR4A/LR4B, the rated values shall be 12 V, 0.75 W (minor) and 3 W (major), and the wattage at 13.5 V DC shall be 1.0 W max. (minor) and 3.5 W max. (major).
requirements.why: Electrical limit of an LR4 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the power per function.

requirements.text: For LR4A/LR4B production light sources, the luminous flux at 13.5 V DC shall be 6 lm ± 20 % (minor) and 80 lm ± 20 % (major), with the major value between 100 and 70 per cent of the 1-minute value, and at 9 V DC shall be 1.5 lm min. (minor) and 19 lm min. (major).
requirements.why: Photometric limit of an LR4 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the flux per function.

requirements.text: For LR4A/LR4B, the major and the minor function shall be operated by separate electrical circuits.
requirements.why: Circuit design of the lamp for an LR4 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the wiring and circuit design.

requirements.text: For LR4A/LR4B, the emitted light shall be red, and in case of failure the current draw between 12 V and 14 V shall be less than 20 mA.
requirements.why: Colour and failure behaviour of an LR4 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the colour and the failure current.

requirements.text: For LR4A/LR4B normal production (box f = 4.5 mm), the flux proportion shall be: minor function area A ≥ 75 %; major function A ≤ 25 %, each B individually ≥ 15 %, A, all B and all C together ≥ 90 %.
requirements.why: Light emitting area of an LR4 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a screen projection per function.

requirements.text: For LR4A/LR4B, the normalized intensities for both major and minor function shall comply with Table 4 for normal production (e.g. 0°: 200-401; ±45°: 142-305; ±90°: 0-38 cd/1000 lm).
requirements.why: Intensity distribution of an LR4 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a goniophotometer measurement per function.

requirements.text: For LR5A/LR5B/LW5A/LW5B, a minimum free air space of 5 mm shall be respected for convection, and the cap shall be PGJ18.5d-10 (LR5) or PGJ18.5d-28 (LW5) in accordance with IEC 60061 (sheet 7004-185-1).
requirements.why: Installation and cap of an L5 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the clearance and gauge the cap.

requirements.text: For LR5A/LR5B, the rated values shall be 12 V / 3 W and the wattage 3.5 W max. at 13.5 V DC, and the luminous flux shall be 120 lm ± 15 % at 13.5 V DC (production) and 28 lm min. at 9 V DC.
requirements.why: Electrical and photometric limit of a red L5 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the power and flux.

requirements.text: The emitted light shall be red for LR5A/LR5B and white for LW5A/LW5B, and in case of failure the current draw between 12 V and 14 V shall be less than 20 mA.
requirements.why: Colour and failure behaviour of an L5 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Measure the colour and the failure current.

requirements.text: For LR5A/LR5B normal production, the flux proportion shall be: each B individually ≥ 10 %; each A, B individually < 40 %; all B together ≥ 60 %; all A, B and C together ≥ 90 %. For LW5A/LW5B: each A, B ≥ 6 % and < 40 %; all A, B together ≥ 55 %; each C < 15 %; all together ≥ 90 %.
requirements.why: Light emitting area of an L5 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a screen projection with the box system (f = 4.5 mm).

requirements.text: For LR5/LW5, the normalized intensities shall comply with Table 4 for normal production (e.g. 0°: 200-425; ±45°: 145-310; ±60°: 85-245; ±90°: 0-70 cd/1000 lm).
requirements.why: Intensity distribution of an L5 source if used.
requirements.test_case: Perform a goniophotometer measurement.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources with integrated heat sink are used, they shall be measured in still air at an ambient temperature of (23 ± 2) °C, and at an additional ambient temperature if indicated in the relevant data sheet of Annex 1, with the minimum free air space defined in the data sheet maintained.
requirements.why: x
requirements.test_case: Check that photometric tests are run in still air at 23 ± 2 °C with the data-sheet free air space.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used in the lamp, production LED light sources shall meet the specified tolerances for production LED light sources in the relevant data sheet of Annex 1 and the relevant data sheet for the caps, so that conformity is satisfied from a photometric, geometrical, visual and electrical standpoint.
requirements.why: Only applies if replaceable R128 LED light sources are fitted; the profile notes replaceability is unconfirmed.
requirements.test_case: Measure production LED light source samples for flux, power, dimensions and cap geometry against the Annex 1 data sheet tolerances for production light sources.

requirements.text: For each type of LED light source, conformity tests in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation shall be carried out at appropriate intervals.
requirements.why: This is a CoP obligation that only applies if the lamp uses approved replaceable LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Audit the CoP test plan and records for each LED light source type to confirm the test frequency.

requirements.text: Conformity tests of the LED light sources shall cover their photometric, geometrical and optical characteristics.
requirements.why: Defines the scope of the CoP checks for any R128 LED light source used in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Review CoP records to confirm that photometric, geometrical and optical characteristics are all tested.

requirements.text: Conformity tests of the LED light sources shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
requirements.why: This test condition constrains how CoP compliance of the LED light sources is demonstrated.
requirements.test_case: Verify that CoP test procedures follow the R128 measurement methods, such as 13.5 V DC and 30 min stabilisation.

requirements.text: Test apparatus used for conformity tests of the LED light sources shall be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a competent authority.
requirements.why: This is a prerequisite for valid CoP measurement of the LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Check calibration certificates and correlation records for the photometric and electrical test equipment.

requirements.text: Samples of LED light sources for conformity testing shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch of LED light sources of the same type.
requirements.why: This sampling condition constrains CoP verification of the LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Review the sampling procedure for random selection within uniform batches.

requirements.text: The LED light sources shall be inspected and test results recorded following the grouping of characteristics as listed in Annex 6, Table 1.
requirements.why: This record grouping applies to the CoP of the R128 LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Check that CoP records are grouped per Annex 6 Table 1, covering marking, dimensions, caps, light emitting area, initial readings, intensity distribution and current.

requirements.text: Compliance shall be assured such that the level of acceptable non-compliance per grouping of characteristics given in Table 1 of Annex 6 is not exceeded.
requirements.why: This sets the CoP acceptance criterion for the production LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Statistically evaluate test results per grouping against the 1 % or 6.5 % acceptable non-compliance levels.

requirements.text: The number of LED light sources not complying with the requirement for any grouping of characteristics of any LED light source type shall not exceed the qualifying limits in the relevant Tables 2, 3 or 4 of Annex 6, each individual LED light source requirement being considered as a characteristic.
requirements.why: These are quantitative CoP limits for the production LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Count non-compliant units per grouping and compare them with the Annex 6 Table 2, 3 or 4 qualifying limit for the sample size.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the manufacturer's test records for marking, legibility and durability shall cover a minimum 12-monthly sample of 315 per grouping (all types with the same external dimensions), with an acceptable level of non-compliance of 1 per cent.
requirements.why: CoP compliance level for LED light sources under R128 if the lamp uses replaceable LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Audit 12-month CoP records for sample size ≥ 315 and non-compliance rate against the 1 % qualifying limits.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the test records for external LED light source dimensions (excluding cap/base) shall cover a minimum 12-monthly sample of 200 per grouping (all types of the same category), with an acceptable level of non-compliance of 1 per cent.
requirements.why: Dimensional CoP level for R128 LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Audit dimensional CoP records for sample size ≥ 200 and non-compliance within the 1 % limit.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the test records for dimensions of caps and bases shall cover a minimum 12-monthly sample of 200 per grouping (all types of the same category), with an acceptable level of non-compliance of 6.5 per cent.
requirements.why: Cap/base CoP level for R128 LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Audit cap/base dimension records for sample size ≥ 200 and non-compliance within the 6.5 % limit.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the test records for dimensions related to the light emitting surface and internal elements shall cover a minimum 12-monthly sample of 200 per grouping (all LED light sources of one type), with an acceptable level of non-compliance of 6.5 per cent.
requirements.why: Emitting-area CoP level for R128 LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Audit light-emitting-surface dimension records for sample size ≥ 200 and non-compliance within the 6.5 % limit.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the test records for initial readings, power, colour and luminous flux shall cover a minimum 12-monthly sample of 200 per grouping (all LED light sources of one type), with an acceptable level of non-compliance of 1 per cent.
requirements.why: Photometric/electrical CoP level for R128 LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Audit power, colour and luminous flux records for sample size ≥ 200 and non-compliance within the 1 % limit.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the test records for normalised luminous intensity or cumulative luminous flux distribution shall cover a minimum 12-monthly sample of 20 per grouping (all LED light sources of one type), with an acceptable level of non-compliance of 6.5 per cent.
requirements.why: Light distribution CoP level for R128 LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Audit goniometric distribution records for sample size ≥ 20 and non-compliance within the 6.5 % limit.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the test records for electrical current shall cover a minimum 12-monthly sample of 20 per grouping (all LED light sources of one type), with an acceptable level of non-compliance of 1 per cent.
requirements.why: Electrical current CoP level for R128 LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Audit electrical current (incl. failure-mode current) records for sample size ≥ 20 and non-compliance within the 1 % limit.

requirements.text: The CoP assessment shall in general cover series production LED light sources from individual factories; records from several factories may only be grouped if they operate under the same quality system and quality management.
requirements.why: Constrains how LED light source production conformity is demonstrated.
requirements.test_case: Check that CoP records are per factory or that grouped factories share the same quality system.

requirements.text: In case an LED light source has more than one light output function, the grouping of characteristics (dimensions, power, colour and luminous flux) shall apply to each element separately.
requirements.why: Applies to dual-function (e.g. stop/position) LED light sources.
requirements.test_case: Verify CoP records for multi-function LED light sources are kept separately for each function element.

requirements.text: For groupings with an acceptable level of 1 per cent of non-compliance, the number of non-compliances shall not exceed the qualifying limits of Table 2 (e.g. 0 for 20 results, 1 for 21-50, 2 for 51-80, 3 for 81-125, 5 for 126-200, 6 for 201-260, 7 for 261-315, up to 21 for 1,191-1,249 results), assuming an acceptance probability of at least 0.95.
requirements.why: Pass/fail acceptance limits for 1 % CoP groupings.
requirements.test_case: Compare counted non-compliances per characteristic against Table 2 for the number of test results.

requirements.text: For groupings with an acceptable level of 6.5 per cent of non-compliance, the number of non-compliances shall not exceed the qualifying limits of Table 3 (e.g. 3 for 20 LED light sources, 5 for 21-32, 7 for 33-50, 10 for 51-80, 14 for 81-125, 21 for 126-200, up to 98 for 1,234-1,249), assuming an acceptance probability of at least 0.95.
requirements.why: Pass/fail acceptance limits for 6.5 % CoP groupings.
requirements.test_case: Compare counted non-compliances per characteristic against Table 3 for the number of LED light sources in records.

requirements.text: For 1,250 or more test results, the non-compliances shall not exceed the qualifying limits of Table 4 expressed as a percentage of results (e.g. 1.68 % / 7.91 % at 1,250; 1.52 % / 7.61 % at 2,000; 1.37 % / 7.29 % at 4,000; 1.23 % / 7.00 % at 10,000; 1.02 % / 6.55 % at 1,000,000 for the 1 % and 6.5 % acceptable levels respectively).
requirements.why: Pass/fail acceptance limits for large CoP record sets.
requirements.test_case: Compute non-compliance percentage of large record sets and compare to Table 4.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, production LED light sources shall meet the specified tolerances for production LED light sources in the relevant data sheet of Annex 1 from a photometric, geometrical, visual and electrical standpoint.
requirements.why: CoP criterion for R128 LED light sources, applicable if the lamp's LED modules are replaceable R128 light sources.
requirements.test_case: Sample production LED light sources and verify dimensions, luminous flux, wattage, colour and failure current against the Annex 1 category sheet production tolerances.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, production LED light sources shall meet the tolerances specified in the relevant data sheet for the caps.
requirements.why: Cap conformity is part of the CoP criterion for R128 LED light sources fitted in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Gauge the cap of sampled production LED light sources against the IEC 60061 cap sheet referenced in the category data sheet.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, the spot-check results of mass-produced LED light sources shall be in agreement with Annex 8, i.e. accepted under the double sampling plan of Table 1 for each grouping of characteristics.
requirements.why: Defines the pass criterion for CoP of mass-produced LED light sources used in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Test a first random sample of 125 LED light sources per grouping of characteristics and check that the number of non-conforming units is within the Annex 8 Table 1 acceptance numbers.

requirements.text: Where replaceable LED light sources are used, production shall be brought into conformity with the requirements if the spot-check results are not in agreement with Annex 8.
requirements.why: Non-conforming CoP results require the production of the LED light sources to be corrected.
requirements.test_case: Review CoP records: where Annex 8 rejection numbers were reached, verify corrective action and conforming retest results.

requirements.text: Where conformity of the LED light sources has been contested, a further sample of 250 LED light sources selected at random from a recent production run shall comply with Annex 8 within two months.
requirements.why: Follow-up CoP sample that the production LED light sources must pass after contested conformity.
requirements.test_case: Test a random sample of 250 LED light sources from recent production within two months and assess acceptance against Annex 8 Table 1.

requirements.text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.why: The rear lamp is a light-signalling device approved under R148 and must provide space for its markings.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp drawing and sample to confirm a marking area large enough for all required markings.

requirements.text: All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.why: This applies to all markings carried by the R148 rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Visually check legibility, then perform a rub or durability test to confirm the markings are indelible.

requirements.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.why: This sets the size constraint for the approval marking on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the approval mark on the sample and confirm it is ≥ 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.why: This defines a required element of the lamp's approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circle enclosing an E and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
requirements.why: This is a required element of the lamp's approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4–6 digit sequential number.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.why: This is a placement constraint on the lamp's marking.
requirements.test_case: Verify on the sample that the sequential number is adjacent to the E-circle.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4 (i.e. R1 or R2 for the rear position lamp, S1 or S2 for the stop lamp, AR for the reversing lamp).
requirements.why: The lamp contains rear position, stop and reversing functions, each identified by a symbol.
requirements.test_case: Check that the marking shows the correct function symbols for each function in the lamp.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. 148R01).
requirements.why: This is a required element of the lamp's approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '148R' followed by the series digits.

requirements.text: On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.why: The wraparound body-side rear combination lamp is likely handed.
requirements.test_case: For a side-specific (handed) lamp, verify a horizontal arrow is present in the marking.

requirements.text: For rear position lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.why: The product includes a rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Check that the arrow on the fitted lamp points to the vehicle outboard side.

requirements.text: For reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.why: The product includes a reversing lamp.
requirements.test_case: If the reversing lamp is approved with reduced distribution, verify the arrow points outwards.

requirements.text: If applicable, to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4, the additional letter "D" shall be marked on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
requirements.why: Rear position or stop lamp functions may be approved as independent-lamp assemblies.
requirements.test_case: If approved as part of a D assembly, check that 'D' is placed right of the function symbol.

requirements.text: If applicable, to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4, the additional letter "Y" shall be marked on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
requirements.why: The rear lamp functions may be realised as an interdependent lamp system.
requirements.test_case: If part of an interdependent lamp system, check that 'Y' is placed right of the function symbol.

requirements.text: On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1 of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.why: Rear position and stop lamps may be approved with reduced light distribution.
requirements.test_case: If the lamp is approved for mounting height ≤ 750 mm with reduced distribution, verify the downward arrow symbol.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.why: This is a direct marking obligation on the R148 lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the presence of the complete approval marking.

requirements.text: Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.why: This is a direct marking obligation on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the trade name or mark.

requirements.text: Lamps with replaceable light sources shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed and, where approved for LED substitute light source(s), the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
requirements.why: It applies only if the LED sources turn out to be replaceable (to be confirmed).
requirements.test_case: If replaceable light sources are used, check that the light source category marking is present.

requirements.text: Lamps with non-replaceable light sources, an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control or a secondary operating mode shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
requirements.why: The lamp uses presumed non-replaceable LED modules on a PCB.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant, the specific identification code of the module ("MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, plus additional symbols where several non-identical modules are used, from the same applicant as the lamp mark), and the rated voltage(s) or range of voltage.
requirements.why: It applies if the LED modules are replaceable light source modules.
requirements.test_case: If replaceable modules are used, inspect each module for the trade name, MD code and voltage.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.why: It applies if the LED modules are replaceable light source modules.
requirements.test_case: If replaceable modules are used, inspect the lamp for the module MD code and voltage.

requirements.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.why: The LED lamp may use separate control electronics.
requirements.test_case: If an external control gear exists, inspect it for the ID number and manufacturer name.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
requirements.why: This sets the marking location requirement for the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Verify the marking location is on the lens or on a part permanently joined to the lens.

requirements.text: The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.why: This is a visibility requirement for the lamp's approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Check marking visibility with the lamp installed on the vehicle (with the boot lid opened if necessary).

requirements.text: If the outer lens of the device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.why: The outer lens is a part of this lamp.
requirements.test_case: If the lens is detachable, verify markings exist on both the lens and the housing.

requirements.text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.why: The outer lens covers several functions of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: If a common lens is used, inspect each main body for only its own function markings.

requirements.text: The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2, 3.3.3.3, 3.3.3.4, 3.3.3.5 (b) and 3.3.3.6 shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.why: This defines where the lamp's markings must be applied.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that these markings are on the lamp itself.

requirements.text: The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5 (a) shall be affixed on the light source module component.
requirements.why: It applies if replaceable light source modules are used.
requirements.test_case: If replaceable modules are used, verify the module markings are on the module.

requirements.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.
requirements.why: The rear combination lamp groups the position, stop and reversing lamps and the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: With the lamp installed, check the single approval mark is visible.
